findings.claim: Swapping the model flips task outcomes more (22% at median) than swapping the harness (13%) or rerunning the same configuration (13%) on the hard45 subset.
Model rankings reverse across harnesses: Claude scores 36/63 vs GPT 31/63 in OpenHands, but PI records 19/63 for Claude and 38/63 for GPT.
Harness equivalence (CC vs mini-SWE within 5 percentage points) holds only for two Qwen models; OpenCode loses up to 9.2 percentage points relative to the other harnesses.

Model contrasts (Opus vs GPT) show wide confidence intervals (Opus -1.25 pp CI [-10,+7.5]; GPT +1.25 pp CI [-4.4,+6.9]) that do not establish equivalence or give a transportable probability of superiority.
OpenCode's harness advantage shrinks from about 6 to 2.67 percentage points as tool calls increase from 39.87 to 72.23.
Across 7 rerun pairs of 5 crossed models, model swaps flip 16% of task outcomes.
